card.title: Say You Missed Me
card.instruction: Get someone to admit longing, jealousy, hurt, or attachment before you reveal your own.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're selling the sofa but keeping my chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody offered anything for it. Have you brought its cushion back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If someone offered twenty pounds, would you still keep it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I like pretending you're about to sit down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll admit I sleep with the cushion. Could you take the price sticker off before I sit?

mechanism: A probes the emotional reason for keeping a chair before admitting their own attachment to the cushion.
confusable: Unlike asking about furniture ownership, A must seek longing beneath a practical explanation and reveal only after it appears.
comparison: D88-b uses a hypothetical price to separate market value from attachment; D88-a uses a remembered key sound to elicit missing someone.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
